ops.statement: The Admiral's harvest-before-sweep substep (constellation-admiral SKILL.md Closeout step 4: 'harvest first, then remove') is enforced only by prose, not by any check. Staging a fenced commander's trio into .agent-work/staged-feedback/<work-id>/ and satisfying that commander's own feedback/archive gate against the staging dir (via verify_agent_feedback.py) proves the trio was COLLECTED out of the worktree; it does not prove the trio was MERGED into the shared durable .agent-work/AGENT_FEEDBACK.md / CONSTELLATION_FEEDBACK.md / LESSONS.md. Those are two separate acts, and a worktree sweep silently drops the run's learning if it happens between them: at epic-601 closeout, 6 of 7 fenced-commander trios (624-phase0, 625-segmentation-substrate, wave4-626, 627-unified-basis, 638-f12-stability-rework, 630-phase6-bt-injection) were collected-but-unmerged, and every one of their source worktrees was already swept before anything caught the gap -- only Ship I/#513 (no fencing exception, wrote the durable files directly) had actually reached the durable log. Found by a human teammate re-checking after closeout, not by any engine gate.
ops.grounding: .agent-work/epic-601/ADMIRAL_LOG.md Closeout section, INCIDENT + FIX entry dated 2026-07-24 (team-lead's finding + manual merge of the 6 missing trios into AGENT_FEEDBACK.md/CONSTELLATION_FEEDBACK.md with provenance comments); C:/Users/fredc/.claude/skills/constellation-admiral/SKILL.md Closeout step 4 (the doctrine text this run violated, already precise -- 'a worktree swept before its trio is collected silently drops that run's learning' -- but backed by nothing that actually checks it); direct diff of .agent-work/staged-feedback/*/AGENT_FEEDBACK.md against .agent-work/AGENT_FEEDBACK.md's pre-fix tail confirmed the 6 trios were absent from the durable file while their worktrees no longer existed.
ops.bank_reason: First observed instance of the harvest ordering actually being violated in practice, even though the doctrine text already states the risk almost verbatim -- re-observe on the next epic that uses fenced commanders whether this recurs (i.e. whether prose-only doctrine keeps failing under closeout time pressure) before deciding the fix must be mechanical (e.g. a verify_agent_feedback.py extension, or a worktree-remove precondition, that cross-checks every staged-feedback/<work-id>/ directory against the durable log's actual content and refuses/warns on a mismatch).
